Present 
Mr. Justice Sheikh Abdul Awal 
Criminal Appeal No. 5224 of 2018 
 
Md. Anowar Hossain and others

Heard on 09.06.2024 and  
Judgment on 10.06.2024 
 
Sheikh Abdul Awal, J: 
 
These two  appeals being Criminal Appeal No. 
5224 of 2018 and Criminal Appeal No. 14293 of 2019 at 

<<PAGE 2>>
 
2
the instance of Md. Anowar Hossain and others are 
directed against the judgment and order of conviction 
and sentence dated 30.04.2018 passed by the learned 
Additional Sessions Judge, 4th Court, Cumilla in 
Sessions Trial Case No. 347 of 2015 arising out of G.R. 
No. 341 of 2014 corresponding to Kotwali Model Police 
Station Case No. 82 dated 24.04.2014 convicting the 
accused-appellants under table 9(Kha) of section 19(1) 
of the Madak Drobbya Niyontron Ain, 1990 and 
sentencing 
them 
thereunder 
to 
suffer 
rigorous 
imprisonment for a period of 5(five) years and to pay a 
fine of Taka 10,000/- (ten thousand) in default to suffer 
simple imprisonment for a period 04 (four) months more 
each and also convicting the accused-appellants under 
table 22(Ga) of the Madak Drobbya Niyontron Ain, 
1990 and sentencing them thereunder to suffer rigorous 
imprisonment for a period of 2(two) years and to pay a 
fine of Taka 2,000/- (two thousand) in default to suffer 
simple imprisonment for a period 04 (four) months more 
each.  
 
Since both the appeals arose from a common  
judgment dated 30.04.2018 passed in Sessions Trial 
Case No. 347 of 2015, they are taken up together for 
hearing and are disposed of by this one judgment. 

<<PAGE 3>>
 
3
 
The prosecution case, in brief, is that one, S.I. 
Abdul Muntakim, DAD, RAB-11 as informant on 
24.04.2014 at about 02:45 hours lodged an Ejahar with 
Kotwali Model Police Station against the accused 
appellants under table 9(Kha)/22(GA) of section 19(1) of 
the Madak Drobbya Niyontron Ain, 1990 stating, inter-
alia, that while the informant along with other RAB  
forces were on special  duty at Courtbari area under 
Kotwali police station  and then at 21:00 hours got a 
secret information that some drug paddlers are selling 
and purchasing drugs in the house of Anwar Hossain of 
village Amtali and thereafter, the informant party 
informed the matter to their  higher authority and as per 
instructions of the higher authority the informant and 
RAB  forces  rushed there while sensing the presence of 
RAB forces the accused persons tried to run away but 
the informant party apprehended accused S.M. Jamal 
Uddin and Helal Uddin  in-front of the house of accused 
Anwar and on search,  recovered 5 bottles of whiskey 
kept in a plastic bag and also recovered 50 yaba tablets 
from accused Jaman and recovered 4 bottles of whiskey 
from the pant pocket of accused Helal. Thereafter, the 
informant party apprehended the accused Anwar Hossain 
from his house and on search, recovered 250 yaba tablets 
from his wearing shirt pocket and also recovered 100 

<<PAGE 4>>
 
4
yaba tablets from accused Surjo Banu kept under her 
kamiz and thereafter, the informant party seized those 
whiskey and yaba tablets by preparing  seizure list in 
presence of local witnesses.  
Upon the aforesaid First Information Report, 
Kotwali Model Police Station Case No. 82 dated 
24.04.2014 under table 9(Kha)/22(Ga) of section 19(1) 
of the Madak Drobbya Niyontron Ain, 1990 was started 
against all 4 accused persons. 
Police after completion of investigation submitted 
charge sheet against the accused-appellants, vide charge 
sheet 
No. 
431 
dated 
02.06.2014 
under 
table 
9(kha)/22(Ga) of section 19(1) of the Madok Drabya 
Niyantran Ain, 1990. 
 
Thereafter, in usual course the case record was sent 
to the Court of learned Sessions Judge, Cumilla, wherein 
it was registered as Sessions Trial Case No. 347 of 2015 
which 
was 
subsequently 
transmitted 
to 
learned 
Additional Sessions Judge, 4th Court, Cumilla for trial 
wherein  the accused-appellants were put on trial to 
answer a  charge under table 9(Kha)/22(Ga) to section 
19(1) of the Madak Drobbya Niyontron Ain, 1990 to 
which the accused-appellants pleaded not guilty and 

<<PAGE 5>>
 
5
claimed to be tried stating that they have been falsely 
implicated in this case. 
 
At the trial the prosecution side has examined in all 
07(seven) witnesses to prove its case, while the defence 
examined none.  
 
The defence case, from the trend of cross-
examination 
of 
the 
prosecution 
witnesses 
and 
examination of the accused-appellants under section 342 
of the Code of Criminal Procedure appeared to be that 
the accused-appellants  were innocent and they have 
been falsely implicated in the case. 
 
On conclusion of trial, the learned Additional 
Sessions Judge, 4th Court, Cumilla by the impugned 
judgment and order dated 30.04.2018 found the accused-
appellants guilty under table 9(Kha) and 22(Ga) of 
section 19(1) of the Madak Drobbya Niyontron Ain, 
1990 and sentenced them as stated above.  
 
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned 
judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 
30.04.2018, the accused-appellants preferred these 2 
criminal appeals.   
 
Ms. Hasina Akter, the learned Advocate appearing 
for the convict-appellants in both the appeals in the 
course of argument takes me through the F.I.R, charge 

<<PAGE 6>>
 
6
sheet, deposition of witnesses and other materials on 
record including the impugned judgment and order of 
conviction and sentence  dated 30.04.2018 and then 
submits that the appellants are innocent,  who have been 
falsely implicated in this case, in-fact,  no incriminating 
drugs were  recovered from the direct possession and 
control of the accused-appellants. She next submits that 
in this case, the prosecution side examined total 7 
witnesses to prove its case out of which PW-1 stated 
nothing against accused Helal and PW-3 stated in his 
deposition that all the drugs were recovered from all 
accused persons which is totally contrary from the FIR 
version as well as deposition of other witnesses, PW-4 
was tendered, PW-5  seizure list witness stated nothing 
as to recovery of yaba tablets and whiskey from the 
direct possession and control of the convict-appellants. 
PW-6 and PW-7 both of them investigated the case and 
finally PW-7 submitted charge sheet against the accused-
appellants, both these witnesses inconsistently deposed 
before the trial Court as to recovery of yaba tablets and 
whiskey from the possession of the convict-appellants 
and in the facts and circumstances of the case the learned 
Judge of the trial Judge ought to have given benefit of 
doubt to the accused-appellants although the trial Court 
below without considering all these aspects of the case   

<<PAGE 7>>
 
7
from a correct angle mechanically passed the impugned 
judgment and order of conviction and sentence against 
the appellants and as such,  the same is liable to be set-
aside.  
 
Ms. Shahida Khatoon, the learned Deputy 
Attorney-General, on the other hand, supports the 
impugned judgment and order of conviction and 
sentence, which was according to her just, correct and 
proper. She submits that in this case the prosecution side 
examined in all 7 witnesses and all of them categorically 
testified that the seized drugs were recovered from the 
possession and control of the convict-appellants and 
thus, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 4th Court, 
Cumilla on due consideration of the evidence on record  
justly found that the accused-appellants guilty under 
table 9(Kha)/22(Ga) to section 19(1) of the Madak 
Drobbya Niyontron Ain, 1990.  
Having heard the learned Advocate and the learned 
Deputy Attorney General, perused the memo of appeal, 
the First Information Report, charge sheet, deposition of 
witnesses and other materials on record including the 
impugned judgment and order of conviction and 
sentence dated 30.04.2018. Now, the only question that 
calls for my consideration in this appeal is whether 
the trial Court committed any error in finding the 

<<PAGE 8>>
 
8
accused-appellants guilty of the offence under table 
9(Kha)/22(GA) of section 19(1) of the Madak Drobbya 
Niyontron Ain, 1990. 
On scrutiny of the record, it appears that the 
prosecution to prove its case examined in all 7 (seven) 
witnesses out of which PW-1, A.S.I, Abdus Shahid, 
member of the raiding party stated in his deposition that 
on the basis of a secret information under the leadership 
of D.A.D. Md. Mostakim he along with other forces 
rushed to the place of occurrence and apprehended the 
accused Anwar Hossain, Surjoban Banu, Helal Uddin, 
S.M. Jamal Uddin and on search, recovered 7 bottles 
whiskey and 50 yaba tablets from accused Jaml Uddin, 4 
bottles whiskey and 250 yaba tablets from accused 
Anwar Hossain and 50 yaba tablets from accused Surjo 
Banu. This witness identified the accused persons on 
dock. In cross examination  the defence failed to find out 
any contradiction in the evidence of P W-1. PW-2, Md. 
Abdul Mustakim, Circle Adjutant, Ansar Battalion, 
informant of the case stated categorically in his 
deposition that on the basis a of secret information he 
along with other forces rushed to the place of occurrence 
and apprehended the accused  persons and on search,  
recovered total 5 bottles whiskey and 50 yaba tablets 
from accused Jaman, 250 yaba tablets from accused 

<<PAGE 9>>
 
9
Anwar and 100 yaba tablets from the wife of accused 
Anwar and thereafter S.I. Asit Kumar prepared seizure 
list as per direction of this witness (informant) in 
presence of the witness. Defence cross-examined this 
witness but failed to find out any contradiction in the 
evidence of this witness. PW-3, S.I. Md. Abdul Latif, 
member of the raiding party gave similar type of  
evidence as like as PW-1 and PW-2 in respect of all 
material particulars. PW-4 was tendered. PW-5, Rubel, 
seizure list witness stated in his respective evidence that- 
“
” PW-6, Md. Ikter Mia partly 
investigated the case. This witness stated in his 
deposition that he examined the witnesses under section 
161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. This witness 
proved the sketch map, index and signature as “Ext.-3, 
3/1.” This witness also proved seized goods as material 
“Exts-I, II”. PW-7, S.I. Md. Saiful Islam stated in his 
deposition that on completion of the investigation he 
found a prima facie case and accordingly submitted 

<<PAGE 10>>
 
10
charge sheet against the accused appellants  and he 
produced the relevant documents as per requirement of 
law, which were marked as exhibits. 
On going through the F.I.R. together with  the 
evidence of PWs, it appears that PW-1, PW-2, PW-3, 
PW-6 and PW-7 all of them in their respective 
deposition categorically stated that the accused-
appellants were apprehended along with the seized 
drugs, all these witnesses deposed that accused 
appellants illegally kept in their  possession the seized 
drugs and all the prosecution witnesses namely, PWs. 1-
4 proved the prosecution case as to the time, place and 
manner of occurrence. 
However, it is found that in this case the accused-
appellants were apprehended along with whiskey as well 
as 50+250+100 = 400 yaba tablets separately and in that 
view of the matter the trial Court ought to have awarded 
sentence to the appellants under table 9(ka) in place of 
table 9(kha) to section 19(1) of the Drobbya Niyontron 
Ain, 1990.  
In this connection certain provisions of law are 
required to be referred to for having a better view of the 
dispute in question.   Tables 9(ka), 9(kha) and 22(Ga) of 

<<PAGE 11>>
 
11
section 19(1) of the Drobbya Niyontron Ain, 1990 which 
reads as follows: 
 
-
Considering the law, facts and circumstances of the 
case as discussed above, particularly  the fact that the 
appellants have already been faced the agony of the 
protracted prosecution and also suffered the mental 
harassment for a long period of one decade, I think that, 
the ends of justice, will be met in the facts and 
circumstances of the case, if the sentence of the 
appellants is reduced to the period of 6 (six) months in 
place of 5 years in view of the provisions of table 9(ka) 

<<PAGE 12>>
 
12
to  section 19(1) of the Drobbya Niyontron Ain, 1990 
and the conviction  and sentence of the accused-
appellants under table 22(Ga) of section 19(1) of the 
Drobbya Niyontron Ain, 1990 is maintained with regard 
to accused-appellants namely, Md. Helal Uddin and 
S.M. Jaman and the conviction and sentence so far as it 
relates to recovery of whiskey under table 22(Ga) of 
section 19(1) of the Drobbya Niyontron Ain, 1990 
against accused appellants namely, Surjo Banu and 
Anwar Hossain is set-aside as  no whiskey was 
recovered from them. 
In the result, therefore, the appeals are allowed in 
part with modification of sentence in the above manner.  
Since both the appeals are allowed in part with 
modification of sentence the convict-appellants are 
directed to surrender their bail bond if so required after 
thorough calculation of their (pre and post trial) 
jail/custody period within 3 (three) months from today to 
suffer rest of the sentence, failing which the trial Court 
shall take necessary steps against the convict-appellants 
to secure their arrest. 
 
Send down the lower Courts’ records at once.
input_summary: PETITIONERs are convicts who appeal against a judgment of an Additional Sessions Judge at Cumilla of 2018, by which they were sentenced under table 9(kha) of section 19(1) of the narcotics statute to five years and a fine, and under table 22(Ga) to two years and a fine, after a rapid action battalion team on special duty stopped their vehicle at Courtbari and recovered foreign liquor and four hundred yaba tablets from them. RESPONDENT is the state. The appeals, heard together, ask that the conviction and the sentences be undone.
explanation: The court found the witnesses consistent as to the time, place and manner of the occurrence, and the recovery of the liquor as well as the tablets established. It held, however, that where the quantity recovered was four hundred yaba tablets, the appropriate entry was table 9(ka) rather than table 9(kha), and it reduced the substantive term accordingly to six months, taking into account the decade the appellants had spent under prosecution. The conviction under table 22(Ga) was affirmed for the two appellants from whose possession liquor was taken and effaced for the other two, no liquor having been recovered from them.

judgment_text:
<<PAGE 1>>
In the Supreme Court of Bangladesh 
High Court Division 
(Civil Revisional Jurisdiction) 
 
Present: 
           
 Mr. Justice Md. Aminul Islam. 
 
Civil Revision No.1177 of 2013.  
 
Tofael Ahmed and another 
                              .........Petitioners. 
                    Vs. 
Ayesha Khatun and others. 
                       ............. Opposite-Parties.   
           
                                       Mrs. Shahana Perveen, Advocate.  
.................. for the petitioners. 
 
 
                  No one appears. 
 
 
 
 
 
      .............for the opposite-parties. 
                                       
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
       
Heard and Judgment on: 12.07.2023.    
 
 
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause 
as to why the order complained of in the petition moved in court today 
should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to 
this Court may seem fit and proper.  
 
The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated 
that the plaintiffs as petitioners filed an Other Suit No.65 of 2012 before the 
learned Court of Joint District Judge, Bandarban defendants as the opposite 
parties in the suit. The plaintiffs purchased the suit land from the defendants 
and they have lost their subsisting interest over the suit land. The plaintiffs 
have got right, title, interest and possessing the same but the defendants on 
various way trying to disturb the plaintiffs possession. The defendants 

<<PAGE 2>>
 
2 
created some forged documents and forcibly tried to evict the petitioners, the 
cause of action arose for filing the suit and thus plaintiffs filed this suit for 
declaration of their title and also prayer for that the registered deed No.23 of 
2009 and 80 of 1981 dated 15.06.2009 and 02.03.1981 are forged, void and 
not binding upon the plaintiffs. Hence , the plaintiffs case.  
 
During pendency of the suit the plaintiffs as petitioners filed an 
application under Order XL Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying 
for appointment of a Receiver in respect of the disputed schedule land on the 
grounds that the plaintiffs filed a suit for declaration of title and recovery of 
khas possession and some registered deed is forged void and not binding 
upon the plaintiffs as petitioners. There is an apprehension of breach of 
peace which might lead to loss of lives between the parties. On the other 
hand, the defendants as opposite parties filed a written objection denying all 
materials on record and the defendants filed Other Suit No.39 of 2008 for 
Specific Performance of Contract and praying for simple declaration. There 
is every possibility for disturbance and litigation between the parties and 
thus the plaintiffs filed an application praying for appointment of a receiver 
in the suit land.  
 
The learned Joint District Judge after hearing both the parties 
considering the materials on record allowed the application for appointment 
of Receiver and who appoint Upazilla Nirbahi Officer as Receiver vide order 
dated 16.10.2012.  

<<PAGE 3>>
 
3 
 
Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid order the 
defendants preferred in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 16 of 2012 before the 
learned District Judge, Bandarban and after hearing the learned Appellate 
Court allowed the application with direction both the parties to maintain 
status-quo in respect of the appointment of Receiver by his order dated 
22.11.2012.  
 
Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order dated 22.11.2012 
the plaintiffs as petitioners preferred in Civil Revision No.1177 of 2013 
before this Court and obtained the instant Rule with granting an ad-interim 
order of stay.  
 
Mrs. Shahana Perveen, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of 
the petitioners while no one appeared on behalf of the opposite party though 
notices were served properly. It is well settled by our Appellate Division 
decided in Safor Uddin Vs. Fazlul Huq, case as reported in 49 DLR(AD) 
151 that a Revision can be disposed of on merit in the absence of either party 
or both the parties. In view of the fact, this is an old case. I am inclined to 
take it up for disposal the Rule on merit in presence of the petitioners.  
 
Mrs. Shahana Perveen, the learned Advocate appearing for the 
petitioners and submits that the learned District Judge has committed an 
error of law occasioning failure of justice in asmuch as the order of status-
quo passed without hearing the petitioners and thus the same is liable to be 
set aside. She further submits that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit 

<<PAGE 4>>
 
4 
land and defendants have also claimed the said portion of land and there is 
every chance of breach of peace in between the parties and thus considering 
all aspects the learned Joint District Judge allowed the prayer for appointing 
as Receiver but the learned District Judge illegally allowed the application 
on 22.11.2012 and to maintain the status-quo till the next date on the issue of 
receiver. She lastly submits that as per provision of Order XL Rule 1 of the 
Code of Civil Procedure, the learned Joint District Judge considering all 
aspects correctly passed the order of receiver but the aforesaid order has 
been stayed by the learned District Judge without giving any opportunity to 
the plaintiffs-petitioners and she prayed for to make the Rule absolute and 
the same is liable to be set aside.  
 
On the other hand, the opposite parties did not appear before this 
Court. Although the notice has been duly served upon the defendants 
opposite parties but they did not engage any lawyer to oppose the Rule. 
 
 In order to appreciate the submissions made by the learned Advocate 
for the petitioners, I have gone through the Revisional application and order 
of the Courts below very carefully.  
 
Now the question calls for consideration whether the learned Judge of 
the Appellate Court below committed any error of law resulting in an error 
in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned order. 
 
On perusal of the record it appears that the plaintiffs as petitioners 
instituted a suit being Other Suit No.65 of 2012 for declaration of their Title 

<<PAGE 5>>
 
5 
and also prayer for that the registered deed No.23 of 2009 and 80 of 1981 
dated 15.06.2009 and 02.03.1981 are forged, void and not binding upon the 
plaintiffs. The defendants Nos.1-13 have no right, title over the same. 
Moreover, the defendants as opposite-parties sold out the schedule land to 
the plaintiffs as petitioners. In this way the plaintiffs as petitioners have got 
right, title, interest and possessing the same but the defendants on various 
way trying to disturb the plaintiffs possession. The defendants created some 
forged documents and forcibly tried to evict the petitioners from the suit 
land. Thereafter, the plaintiffs filed an application under Order XL Rule 1 of 
the Code of Civil Procedure praying for appointment of Receiver. The 
learned trail Court allowed the application and appointed Upazilla Nirbahi 
Officer as receiver.  
 
Scrutinizing the impugned order, relevant papers and all documents, it 
is obvious to note that admittedly, the original Suit No.65 of 2012 was filed 
before the learned Joint District Judge, Bandarban for declaration of title and 
recovery of khas possession in the suit land. On the other hand, the 
defendants as opposite parties instituted Other Suit No.39 of 2008 for 
Specific Performance of Contract with simple declaration. The plaintiffs 
claimed that they have got right, title and possession in the suit land but the 
plaintiffs as petitioners were evicted on 11.09.2011 from the schedule land. 
On the other hand, the defendants opposite parties claimed that the original 
owner of Meher Ali transferred the property on 02.03.1981 to the 

<<PAGE 6>>
 
6 
predecessor of the defendants as opposite parties by way of Affidavit. 
Though the plaintiffs as petitioners instituted a Suit No.65 of 2012 for 
declaration of title and recovery of khas possession .  
 
During pendency of the suit, the petitioners filed an application for 
appointment of a receiver on 16.10.2012 and after hearing the learned Joint 
District Judge, Bandarban allowed the application and appointed Upazilla 
Nirbahi Officer as Reciever. Therefore, the defendants as opposite parties 
filed a Miscellaneous Appeal No.16 of 2012 against impugned the order 
dated 16.10.2012 before the learned District Judge, Bandarban who admitted 
the Appeal as well as called for the Lower Court Record (L.C.R) and the 
next date was fixed on 22.01.2013 for L.C.R. for appeal hearing. In the 
meantime, the defendants as opposite parties filed an application praying for 
stay by order dated 19.11.2012.The learned Joint District Judge fixed on 
22.01.2023 for further hearing. 
 
 It further appears that the learned District Judge by order dated 
19.11.2012 fixed on 22.01.2013 for hearing subject to availability of 
L.C.R.But the defendants-appellant-opposite parties on 22.11.2012 filed an 
application for staying the earlier order of appointing the Receiver .It 
appears that the copy of the said application was not served upon the 
plaintiffs-petitioners, resultantly the petitioners were not given any 
opportunity of submitting objection against the said application for stay .The 

<<PAGE 7>>
 
7 
learned Judge of the lower Appellate Court below only hearing the 
defendants-Appellants passed an order of status-quo till next date.  
 
It further appears that the learned District Judge allowed the 
application without giving any opportunity to the petitioners passed an order 
of status-quo as to appointment receiver of which appears violation of the 
principle of natural justice. The learned Appellate Court below most illegally 
and arbitrary allowed the application and thereby committed an error of law 
resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.  
 
It further appears that the order of stay granted earlier by this Court on 
29.04.2013 against the order of status-quo passed by the Appellate Court 
below dated 22.11.2012 which is prevailing from the very beginning but 
both the parties did not any step for hearing in the instant Rule. In the 
meantime more than 11 years elapsed in disposal for appointment of 
receiver.  
 
In view of the discussions made above, I am to hold that the order 
passed the Appellate Court below is not based on correct evaluation of the 
facts and circumstances of the case for which it needs interference by this 
Court.  
 
However, I find merit in this Rule.  
 
In the result, the Rule is made absolute.  

<<PAGE 8>>
 
8 
 
The impugned order of status-quo dated 22.11.2012 passed by the 
learned District Judge, Bandarban in Miscellaneous Appeal No.16 of 2012 is 
hereby set aside.  
 
However, there will be no order as to cost. The order of stay granted 
earlier by this Court is hereby recalled and vacated.  
 
The learned District Judge, Bandarban is directed to dispose of the 
Miscellaneous Appeal on merit within 6(six) months from the date of receipt 
of the judgment and order positively.  
 
Let the copy of the judgment and order be sent to the Court concerned 
at once. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Md. Abadul Haque/ Bench Officer.
input_summary: PETITIONERs are plaintiffs who sued in Bandarban for a declaration of title and recovery of possession over land they say they bought, together with a declaration that two registered deeds of 1981 and 2009 are forged and not binding on them. They applied for a receiver over the land, apprehending a breach of the peace. The trial court appointed a receiver, and the appellate court, hearing the defendants' application for a stay without notice to the plaintiffs, directed the parties to hold the existing position. RESPONDENTs are the defendants. The plaintiffs seek reversal of that order.
explanation: The court found that the defendants' application for a stay of the receivership order had never been served on the plaintiffs, who were thus denied any opportunity of objecting to it, and that the appellate judge had made the order on hearing the defendants alone. It held that this offended the plainest rule of natural justice and that the order, resting on no correct evaluation of the facts, could not stand. The rule therefore succeeded, the order of November 2012 was effaced, and the appellate court was directed to decide the appeal on its merits within six months.

<<PAGE 1>>
In the Supreme Court of Bangladesh 
High Court Division 
(Civil Revisional Jurisdiction) 
 
Present:  
Mr. Justice Md. Aminul Islam. 
Civil Revision No.1479 of 2005.    
 
 
 
Alhaz Kazi Abdul Oadud 
 
 
 
 
 
                           ……..Plaintiff-Petitioner. 
-VS- 
 
 
 
Md. Abu Taher and others.  
                 …....... Defendant-Opposite-Parties. 
No one appears.  
       ......................….For the petitioner. 
 
 
Mr. Mohammad Abul Hasan, A.A.G. with 
 
 
Ms. Rawsan Ara Rahman, A.A.G. 
 
 
 
       .......................For the opposite-party Nos.2-5. 
 
               
 
 
 
 
Heard on: 14.05.2024 and  
Judgment on: 15.05.2024. 
 
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-party No.1-5 to show 
cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 16.04.2005 passed 
by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Civil Revision No.129 of 2005 
allowing the Revision and Reversing the judgment and order dated 
28.02.2005 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in 
Title Suit No.50 of 2005 allowing the application for mandatory injunction 
filed by the plaintiff-petitioner, should not be set aside and/or pass such 
other or further order or orders passed to this Court may seem fit and proper. 
The case of the plaintiff-petitioner, in short is that the Bangladesh 
Book Publishers and Sellers Association is a commercial institution and the 
same is being managed and guided by the Trade Organization Ordinance, 

<<PAGE 2>>
 
2
1961 and the plaintiff is one of the members of it.  The Government issued a 
circular on 31.07.2002 as per power conferred upon it by the Trade 
Organization Ordinance, 1961 which has the binding force upon the 
Bangladesh Book Publishers and Sellers Association. As per provision of 
the said circular the election of the office bearers of the executive committee 
of the said association was held on 18.12.2003 and 30.12.2003 and the result 
was declared on 04.01.2003 and as per circular the executive committee of 
the said association was elected for a period of 2(two) years and accordingly 
the tenure of the said executive committee has been expired on 03.01.2005 
and the executive committee has failed to conduct the election for the next 
term within 15(fifteen) days before the expiry of the terms of the executive 
committee as per provision of clause 1(4) of the said circular and 
accordingly as per provision of 1(5) of the said circular the executive 
committee would be deemed to have been discharged and the executive 
committee is no more in existence and as per provision of clause 1(6) of the 
said circular the Government is in conclusive obligation to appoint an 
administrator to perform the function of the Executive Committee of the 
Bangladesh Book Publishers and Sellers Association. On 06.12.2004 the 
plaintiff filed an application to the Government to appoint an administrator 
and consequently  a 7(seven) days show cause notice has been served upon 
the president of the executive committee of the said association but failed to 
take any positive step. Subsequently, the defendant No.4 issued a letter 
asking the parties to held a meeting in his office room to have a solution in 

<<PAGE 3>>
 
3
the stated premises and in the said notice he also addressed one Md. Abu 
Taher as the president of the Bangladesh Book Publishers and Sellers 
Association which is illegal and beyond his authority and the Government 
can do nothing but to appoint an administrator to take a decision for 
conducting election of the executive committee of the said association for 
the year 2004-2006. Hence, the case. 
During pendency of the suit the plaintiff-petitioner on 17.02.2005 
filed an application for mandatory injunction under section 151 of the Code 
of Civil Procedure praying for a direction upon the defendants-appellants to 
appoint an administrator for performing the function of the executive 
committee of the Bangladesh Book Suppliers and Sellers Association. After 
hearing the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka issued a show 
cause notice upon the defendants within 7(seven) days. Though the show 
cause notice has been duly served upon the defendants but the defendants 
did not appear before the trial Court. Thereafter, on 28.02.2005 the plaintiff-
petitioner filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil 
Procedure before the learned trial Court. After hearing the learned Court was 
pleased to allow the aforesaid application and thereby directed upon the 
defendants-opposite parties No.2-5 to appoint an administrator for 
performing the function of the executive committee of the Bangladesh Book 
Publishers and Sellers Association within 1(one) month.  
Thereafter, the defendants-opposite parties No.1-5 appeared before 
the learned trial Court and filed an application under section 151 of the Code 

<<PAGE 4>>
 
4
of Civil Procedure praying for recalling the order dated 28.02.2005 and 
staying the operation of the same. In the meantime one Md. Abu Taher 
(opposite party No.1) filed an application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code 
of Civil Procedure for adding him as defendant. On 23.03.2005 the learned 
trial Court has taken up for hearing the matter and after hearing both the 
parties the learned Court was allowed the aforesaid application under Order 
1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for adding party as defendant and 
another application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for 
recalling the order of mandatory injunction dated 28.02.2005 was rejected.  
Being aggrieved  by and dissatisfied with the order dated 28.02.2005 
passed by the learned Court of Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka the 
added defendant-opposite party No.1 preferred Miscellaneous Appeal 
No.108 of 2005 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka. Subsequently, the 
aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeal has been converted to Civil Revision 
No.129 of 2005.  
On 16.04.2005 after hearing both the parties the learned District 
Judge, Dhaka allowed the Civil Revisional and set aside the order dated 
28.02.2005 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka.  
Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned Judgment and 
order dated 16.04.2005 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka the 
plaintiff-opposite party-petitioner has preferred the Civil Revision before 
this Court under Section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure and the leave 
was granted and obtained the Rule with granting an ad-interim order of stay.  

<<PAGE 5>>
 
5
During pendency of this Rule, on 25.05.2005 the added defendant 
opposite party No.01 namely, Md. Abu Taher appeared before this Court 
and with filed an application for vacating the order of stay dated 30.04.2005 
granted by this Court and after hearing the Hon’ble High Court the earlier 
order of stay was vacated.  
This matter has been appearing in the daily cause list with the name of 
the learned Advocate for the petitioners as well as the opposite-parties in a 
couple of days but no one appeared on behalf of the petitioner as well as 
opposite party No.01 to press the Rule. It is well settled by our Appellate 
Division decision the case of Safor Uddin Vs. Fazlul Huq, reported in 49 
DLR(AD) 151 that a Revision can be disposed of on merit in the absence of 
either party or both the parties. In view of the facts this an old case, I am 
inclined to take up for disposal on merit considering the materials on record. 
 The petitioner claimed that the learned District Judge misconceived 
and misconstrued the contents of the application, the proprietary application 
of laws to that effect and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an 
error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned 
judgment and order. The learned Judge failed to appreciate that the 
maintainability of a suit is bundle of fact and for the assignment of the same 
the Court is required to consider the whole pleadings (though yet no written 
statement has been filed), the act of the parties (whether bonafide or 
malafide) and the proprietary application of the concerned laws and in 
disposing of an injunction application the Court is not in a position to decide 

<<PAGE 6>>
 
6
the maintainability of a suit and thus the learned District Judge was wrong in 
holding that the injunction order is not sustainable as the suit is not 
maintainable and thereby the learned District Judge committed an error of 
law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in 
allowing the revisional application by setting aside the injunction order 
granted by the learned trial Court. He further claimed that the learned 
District Judge failed to appreciate that admittedly the tenure of the elected 
executive committee of the Bangladesh Book Publishers and Sellers 
Association has already been expired on 03.01.2005 and as per provision of 
clause 1(5) of the circular dated 31.07.2002 the executive committee is no 
more in existence and as per clause 1(6) of the said circular the Government 
is in exclusive obligation to appoint an Administrator to that effect and 
thereby the learned District Judge committed an error of law resulting in an 
error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in allowing the revisional 
application by setting aside the injunction order granted by the learned trial 
Court. The learned District Judge failed to appreciate that the contesting 
defendant opposite party Nos.2-5 have not been made party in the 
Revisional application and the application for adding them as opposite 
parties in the revision has subsequently been not pressed by the defendant 
opposite party No.1 (the petitioner of the Revisional application) and thus 
the Civil Revision suffers from the defect of parties and the same is not 
tenable in the eye of law and thereby the learned District Judge committed 
an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of 

<<PAGE 7>>
 
7
justice in allowing the Revisional application by setting aside the injunction 
order granted by the learned trial Court. Hence, the Rule is liable to be made 
absolute.  
On the other hand, the opposite party claimed that section 10 of the 
Trade Organization Ordinance, 1961 confers power upon the Government to 
appointment an administrator for a trade organization in certain 
circumstances. And also explained that under section 10 of the Trade 
Organization Ordinanc, the Government may appoint an administrator to 
take over management of a trade organization in supersession of its 
executive committee only if the Government is of the opinion that the 
circumstances and state of affairs set out in the said section are present and 
under no circumstances the Government may appoint an administrator 
without giving the executive committee an opportunity of hearing. From the 
impugned order it is apparent that the Government did not form the 
‘opinion’ but it passed the order under section 10 as directed by the court of 
4th Assistant Judge, Dhaka. The Senior Assistant Judge is not the 
Government. So the order is ex-facie illegal and malafide.  
 
The present Board of Director of petitioner’s Samity has been 
discharging in function since its taking over the charge and at present there 
is no circumstances or state of affairs in the petitioner’s Samity that could 
call for or justify appointment of an administrator to take over management 
of the Samity. It is palpably apparent from the order of appointment of 
Administrator dated 28.02.2005 that the Government has obtained the order 

<<PAGE 8>>
 
8
of injunction in order to create an avenue to interfere into the affairs of the 
Samity.  
 
He further claimed that the Government has acted illegally and 
without any lawful authority in appointing an administrator to take over 
management of the Samity with reference to the order of the Court bellow 
without forming any opinion or being satisfied that any one of the 
circumstances existed in the Samity that might call for appointment of 
administrator inasmuch as under section 10 of the Trade Organization 
Ordinance, 1961 the Government can appoint an administrator only when 
the Government is of the opinion that one of the circumstances or state of 
affairs is present in relation to a trade organization. He further claimed that 
the learned District Judge passed the judgment and order dated 16.04.2005 
considering the actual facts and circumstances and citing the section 12 of 
Trade Organization Ordinance, 1961. According to section 12 of Trade 
Organization Ordinance, 1961 there is bar of suit or other legal proceedings 
without referred the dispute in the Arbitration Tribunal of Federation of 
Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industry and as such the Rule is 
liable to be discharged.   
 
Mr. Mohammad Abul Hasan, the learned Assistant Attorney General 
on behalf of the opposite party Nos.2-5 appeared before this Court and 
submits that the opposite party No.1 is a president of the Bangladesh Book 
Publishers and Sellers Association and he declared the election schedule on 
24.06.2005 for the year 2005-2008. Thereafter, final voter list was prepared 

<<PAGE 9>>
 
9
and published. So, the total election process has been completed and as such 
the Rule is liable to be discharged.  
Scrutinizing the relevant papers and documents it is obvious to note 
that the Bangladesh Book Publishers and Sellers Association is a 
commercial institution and the same is being managed and guided by the 
Trade Organization Ordinance, 1961 and the plaintiff is one of the members 
of it that the Government issued a circular on 31.07.2002 as per power 
conferred upon it by the Trade Organization Ordinance, 1961 which has 
binding force upon the Bangladesh Book Publishers and Sellers Association. 
On 06.12.2004 the plaintiff filed an application to appoint an administrator 
before the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka and 
consequently, show cause notice has been served upon the president of the 
Executive Committee of the said Association and the aforesaid Association 
failed to take any positive step. The defendant No.4 issued a letter asking the 
parties to hold a meeting in his office Room to have a solution in the stated 
premises and the said notice he also addressed one Md. Abu Taher as the 
president of the Bangladesh Book Publishers and Sellers Association which 
is illegal and beyond his authority. On the other hand, the name of the 
Bangladesh Book Publishers and Sellers Samity was changed as into its 
present name, Bangladesh Publishers and Book Sellers Association. The 
Government by the order under memo No.Com/TOT-49/85/239 dated 
12.06.1985 approved the name.  Since the said incorporation and issuance of  
Licence of Association was functioning properly as per its Memorandum 

<<PAGE 10>>
 
10
and Article of Association the law of the country. The Government is 
making regular correspondence with the petitioner’s Samity. The opposite 
party is the elected president of the aforesaid Association which the election 
was held on 28.12.2004 for the terms 2002-2004. The Government 
nominated representative by the order dated 27.10.2002 to supervise the 
election. Thereafter, the executive committee took resolution in their 
meeting and after discussions the decision was taken that the tenure of the 
executive committee will be 3 years instead of 2 years. The matter has been 
decided for amendment of Memorandum and Article of Association and was 
sent to the Director, Trade Organization, Ministry of Commerce, 
Government of Bangladesh for approval under the signature of President, 
Bangladesh Publishers and Book Sellers Association vide memo No. 
Pustuk/2004/347 dated 31.07.2004. The president of the opposite-party 
No.01 Samity sent a letter regarding the announcement of election schedule 
on 24.06.2005  for the year 2005-2008 drawing attention of the Director, 
Trade Organization vide letter No. Pustuk/2005/43 dated 08.02.2005 and 
final voter list was prepared and published. The election process is clearly 
showing under section 10 of the Trade Organization Ordinance, 1961 the 
Government as follows:  
Section 10 of the Trade Organization Ordinance, 1961 confers power 
upon the Government to appoint an administrator for a trade organization in 
certain circumstances. Section 10 of the Trade Organization Ordinance reads 
as follows: 

<<PAGE 11>>
 
11
1) Where the Government is of opinion that the affairs of a registered 
trade organization are not being properly managed and that the 
interests of trade and industry so require, it may, by order in 
writing, supersede the Executive Committee of such trade 
organization for such period, not exceeding one year, as may be 
specified in the order; 
Provided that no such order shall be made unless the Executive 
Committee has been given a notice in writing of and afforded an 
opportunity to make a representation against, the intended 
supersession.  
2) Where..... 
(a) an Executive Committee is superseded under subsection (1), or 
(b) it is not, in the opinion of the (Government), possible for any 
reason to reconstitute the Executive Committee at the due time 
of such reconstitution, or 
(c)  the Executive Committee is debarred, by an order of any Court, 
from discharging its functions, the Government may appoint, 
for such period, not exceeding one year, as it may think fit, an 
Administrator to take over the functions of such Committee and 
to manage and conduct the affairs of the trade organization: 
Provided that if the period of supersession is terminated or the 
Executive Committee is reconstituted or the order of the Court 
is vacated before the expiry of the period for which the 

<<PAGE 12>>
 
12
Administrator shall have been appointed, the Government may 
direct the Administrator to relinquish the functions taken over 
by him in favour of the Executive Committee. 
 
(3) Upon the appointment of an administrator under clause (a) or 
clause (b) of sub-section (2), the members of the Executive Committee shall 
be deemed to have vacated their respective offices and no such member shall 
act or transact any business after such appointment.  
 
From plain reading, as per Trade Organization Ordinance, 1961, the 
Executive Committee, the announcement of the election schedule held on 
24.06.2005 for the year of 2005-2008 and final voter list was prepared and 
published. There is no Embargo in the Election process. Therefore, the total 
election process has already been completed as well as on 25.05.2005 the 
earlier order of stay was vacated. So, the Rule has become infructuous.  
 
Having regard to the facts and circumstances as discussed above I am 
to hold that the impugned judgment and order dated 28.02.2005 passed by 
the learned District Judge, Dhaka rightly and correctly allowing the 
Revision. There is no illegality and infirmity or misreading or non reading 
evidence or non consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the 
decision occasioning failure of justice by which it can be interfered by this 
Court. 
 
Therefore, I find no merit in this Rule.  
In the result, the Rule is discharged. 

<<PAGE 13>>
 
13
 
The impugned judgment and order dated 16.04.2005 passed by the 
learned District Judge, Dhaka in Civil Revision No.129 of 2005 is hereby 
affirmed. 
However, there will be no order as to cost.  
Communicate the judgment and order immediately at once. 
 
 
 
 
 
Md. Abadul Haque/Bench Officer.
input_summary: PETITIONER is a member of an association of book publishers and sellers, registered as a trade organisation, who sued for a mandatory injunction after the executive committee's two-year term expired without a fresh election and the government moved to appoint an administrator. The trial court directed that the committee be restored, and the revisional court undid that direction. RESPONDENTs are rival office bearers and the government. The petitioner seeks restoration of the trial order, contending that the committee had become defunct by operation of the election circular and that the process of reconstitution had begun.
explanation: The court examined the election circular and the statute and found that the election schedule for the new term had already been published, the final voter list prepared, and the whole election process completed, with the earlier stay meanwhile vacated, so that nothing survived for adjudication in the rule. It found no illegality, misreading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts in the revisional order, and no ground on which the discretion exercised below could be disturbed. The rule therefore failed and the revisional order was affirmed, though without any order as to costs.

Sheikh Abdul Awal, J: 
 
 
This Appeal at the instance of convict appellant, 
Dr. Md. Shawkat Rashid is directed against the judgment 
and order of conviction and sentence dated 30.08.2015 
passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Special Sessions 
Court No.2, Rajshahi in Metro. Sessions Case No. 41 of 
2014 arising out of C.R. Case No. 311 of 2013

2
convicting the appellant under section 138 of the

thereunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period 
of 1 (one) year and to pay a fine of Tk. 8,00,000/- (Eight 
lakhs) in default to suffer imprisonment for a period of 2 
(two) months more.  
The gist of the case is that one, Dr. Md. Anowarul 
Haque as complainant filed a petition of complaint being 
C.R. Case No. 311 of 2013 in the Court of the learned 
Chief Metropolitan, Rajshahi against the convict-
appellant under section 138 of the Negotiable 
Instruments Act, 1881 stating, inter-alia, that the 
accused-appellant took loan 
amounting 
to 
Taka 
4,00,000/- from the complainant. Thereafter, in order to 
pay the loan money the convict-appellant on 03.10.2012 
issued a cheque of Tk. 4,00,000/- (Four lakhs) of United 
Commercial Bank Ltd., Rajshahi Branch bearing No. 
6335574 in favour of complainant and on 15.01.2013 the 
complainant presented the said cheque before the bank 
for encashment, which was returned unpaid for 
insufficient of fund and thereafter, 05.02.2013 the 
complainant published a legal notice in the daily 
newspaper namely, “Dainik Barta” asking him  to pay 
the cheque’s amount within 30 days but the accused-
appellant did not pay any heed to it and hence, the case. 

<<PAGE 3>>
 
3
On receipt of the petition of complaint, the learned   
Judicial Magistrate, cognizance Court examined the 
complainant under Section 200 of the Code of Criminal 
Procedure and took cognizance against the accused-
appellant under section 138 of the Negotiable 
Instruments Act, 1881 and issued summon against the 
accused-appellant fixing next date on 27.06.2013.  
Thereafter, in usual course the case record was sent 
to the Court of the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 
Rajshahi, wherein the case was registered as Metro. 
Sessions Case No. 41 of 2014 which was subsequently 
transmitted to the Court of the learned Sessions Judge, 
Special Sessions Court No.2 for disposal in which the 
accused-appellant was put on trial to answer a charge 
under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 
1881.  
At the trial the complainant examined in all 3 
witnesses and also exhibited some documents to prove 
his case and the defence examined 2 witnesses. 
On conclusion of trial, the learned Sessions Judge, 
Special Sessions Court No.2, Rajshahi by the impugned 
judgment and order dated 30.08.2015 convicted the 
accused-appellant under Section 138 of the Negotiable 
Instrument Act, 1881 and sentenced him thereunder to 

<<PAGE 4>>
 
4
suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of 1 (one) year 
and to pay a fine of Tk. 8,00,000/- (Eight lakhs) in 
default to suffer simple imprisonment for a period of 2 
(two) months more.  
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned 
judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 
30.08.2015, the convict-appellant preferred this criminal 
appeal. 
Ms. Mahfuza Akter, the learned Advocate for the 
appellant submits that she is not in a position to make 
argument for the appellant, who is fugitive from law and 
justice. 
Having heard the learned Advocate for both the 
sides, perused the memo of appeal, deposition of 
witnesses and other materials on record including the 
impugned judgment and order of conviction and 
sentence dated 30.08.2015. 
On scrutiny of the record, it appears that the 
complainant filed the petition of complaint being C.R 
Case No. 311 of 2013 in the Court of the learned Chief 
Metropolitan Magistrate, Rajshahi against the convict-
appellant under section 138 of the Negotiable 
Instruments Act, 1881 and during trial the complainant 

<<PAGE 5>>
 
5
side examined 3 witnesses and the defence side

On perusal of record, it is found that the 
complainant-respondent No. 2 after exhausting all the 
legal formalities filed C.R. case No. 311 of 2013 under 
section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act against 
the convict appellant. 
To constitute an offence under Section 138 of the 
N.I. Act, the following elements need to be fulfilled: 
 
1. A cheque should have been issued by the payer 
for the discharge of a debt or other liability. 
 
2. The cheque should have been presented or 
deposited by the payee within a period of six months 
from the date of drawing of the cheque or within the 
period of validity of the cheque, whichever is earlier. 
 
3. The payee should have issued a notice in writing 
to the payer within 30 days of receipt of information 
regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid from the 
bank. 
4. The payer/drawer of the cheque should have 
paid the cheque amount within 30 days of receipt of the 
said notice from the payee. 

<<PAGE 6>>
 
6
5.  If the payer is failed to pay in time the cheque 
amount, the payee should have filed a complaint within 
one month. 
 
On an overall consideration of the facts, 
circumstances and the materials on record, it can be 
easily suggested that all the above quoted key elements 
are exist in the present case. Besides, it appears from the 
record that a single bench of this Court at the time of 
admission of appeal by order dated 17.09.2015 granted 
bail to the convict-appellant for a period of 06(six) 
months and thereafter, no one took any step to extend the

expired long before on 17.03.2016. Therefore, in the 
attending facts and circumstances of the case, I find no 
difficulty whatever in holding that the convict-appellant 
is a fugitive from law and justice. 
In the case of Anti-Corruption Commission Vs. Dr. 
HBM Iqbal Alamgir, reported in 15 BLC(AD) 44, it has 
been held that the Court would not act in aid of an 
accused person, who is a fugitive from law and justice. 
On an analyses of impugned judgment and order of 
conviction and sentence dated 30.08.2015, passed by the 
learned Sessions Judge, Special Sessions Court No.2, 
Rajshahi, I find no flaw in the reasonings of the trial 

<<PAGE 7>>
 
7
Court or any ground to assail the same inasmuch as all 
the key elements of Section 138 of Negotiable 
Instruments Act are exist in the case. 
The learned Sessions Judge, Special Sessions Court 
No.2, Rajshahi appears to have considered all the 
material aspects of the case and justly passed the 
impugned judgment and order of conviction and 
sentence dated 30.08.2015.  
On the above, 2 (two) counts, this appeal must fail.    
In the result, the appeal is dismissed. The 
impugned judgment and order of conviction and 
sentence dated 30.04.2015 passed by the learned 
Sessions Judge, Special Sessions Court No.2, Rajshahi in 
Metro. Sessions Case No. 41 of 2014 arising out of C.R. 
Case No. 311 of 2013 against the accused appellant is 
hereby affirmed.

<<PAGE 8>>
 
8

preferring this Criminal Appeal.

input_summary: PETITIONER was convicted in Narsingdi in 2018 under section 10 of the statute on violence against women and children, as amended in 2003, and under section 323 of the Penal Code, and sentenced to three years' rigorous imprisonment with a fine and to three months' simple imprisonment, the terms to run concurrently, on the complaint of a schoolgirl that he and others had entered her house and assaulted her after she spurned their advances. RESPONDENT is the state. He appeals, contending that the witnesses contradicted each other and that the report was lodged long after the occurrence.
explanation: The court found that the occurrence was said to have taken place on 22 August 2010 but that the complaint was filed on 4 September 2010 with no reasonable explanation for the interval, and held that unexplained delay of that kind corrodes the credibility of the prosecution story. It further found the evidence of the witnesses to be riddled with discrepancies, contradictions and improbable versions, leaving several gaps and doubts as to the appellant's involvement. Holding that the tribunal ought to have extended the benefit of the doubt, it acceded to the appeal, effaced the conviction and sentence, and released the appellant from his bail bond.

input_summary: PETITIONERs are defendants in three connected title suits over the same land in Chuadanga, two brought by the heirs of a former co-sharer for a permanent injunction and recovery of possession and one for partition. The trial court turned down the first two and decreed the partition suit in their favour, and the appellate court reversed all three in a single judgment. RESPONDENTs are the rival claimants. The defendants seek restoration of the trial decrees, contending that the appellate judgment is no proper judgment of reversal and rests on a misquotation of what the trial judge had found.
explanation: The court found that the trial judge had disbelieved the documents of settlement not because they had not been exhibited or signed by the court, as the appellate judgment suggested, but because they had not been signed by the prescribed officer and had not been proved through their lawful custodian, so that the appellate court had misquoted and misread the judgment under appeal. It held that a judgment of reversal must displace the findings it reverses, and that this one did not satisfy the requirements of Order 41 rule 31 of the Code. All three rules succeeded and the trial decrees were restored.

obligation not to grant any injunction against the government or 
any institute of public authority,  if such order is in any way will

input_summary: PETITIONER is a contractor who held the lease of a landing station and labour handling point of the inland water transport authority for 2021-2022, and who sued for compensation of about ninety-five lakh taka after the authority, having assured renewal, put the lease out to tender instead. He obtained an order that the parties hold the existing position, and the appellate court undid that order, holding that a status quo order, being an injunction, could not be passed against a public authority on the day the suit was filed without hearing it. RESPONDENTs are the authority. He seeks reversal.
explanation: The court agreed that the status quo order, passed against a statutory public authority on the very day of filing and without hearing it or any law officer, could not be sustained, and that the appellate court had committed no illegality in undoing it. It also found that the trial judge had travelled far beyond what was called for and made remarks that practically frustrated the suit, which was still at the pleading stage. Those observations of the appellate court on the merits were expunged so that the trial court could form an independent opinion, the rule failed, and the suit was to be concluded quickly.

input_summary: PETITIONERs are the heirs of a landowner who had obtained a rule against an order of the District Judge at Habiganj of 2001 declining to add a party in a title appeal under Order 1 rule 10 of the Code. While the rule was pending the main suit was disposed of, a fact reported to this court by the petitioners' advocate, and a further connected civil rule stood with it. The petitioners seek a decision on the addition of party, contending that the order was wrong. RESPONDENTs are the other side in the appeal.
explanation: The court noted from the statement of the petitioners' own advocate that the main suit out of which the appeal and the addition of party arose had already been disposed of, so that nothing remained to which an order adding a party could attach. On that footing it held that the rule, and the connected civil rule that travelled with it, had been rendered academic by the disposal of the suit. No occasion arose for examining the correctness of the order of 2001. The rule was closed on that ground, and the interim stay was recalled.

input_summary: PETITIONER is a plaintiff who sued in Sylhet for a declaration that the cancellation of a power of attorney of 2020 is not binding on him. The defendant filed a written statement but then stayed away for long, and the trial court, after recording the plaintiff's witnesses, fixed the suit for an ex parte hearing. Before that date the defendant applied to have the suit withdrawn from the ex parte list, and the trial court permitted him to contest on payment of costs of one thousand taka; the revisional court affirmed that. RESPONDENTs are the defendants. The plaintiff seeks reversal.
explanation: The court examined the order and found that the defendant had filed a written statement, that the suit had been put on the ex parte list only because he was absent on some dates, and that the court had permitted him to contest on payment of a small sum in costs. It held that no suit should be decided without affording an opportunity to a party who wishes to contest it, and that the orders of the courts below disclosed no illegality. The leave sought was accordingly declined and the order was affirmed, with a direction that the suit be disposed of quickly.

input_summary: PETITIONERs are defendants in a suit in Chattogram in which the plaintiffs seek a declaration that a decree of 2003 in an earlier suit is illegal and not binding on them. The defendants applied under section 10 of the Code for the suit to be held over until two proceedings then pending in this court, a civil revision and a writ petition, were decided, and the trial court declined; the revisional court affirmed that. RESPONDENTs are the plaintiffs. The defendants seek leave to have both orders undone, contending that the suits overlap.
explanation: The court noted that the civil revision out of which the request for a stay arose had since been decided by a division bench, so that there was no longer any proceeding before this court to await, and that the writ petition still pending arose out of a revenue matter unconnected with the subject matter of the suit. It observed that the order declining a stay had contained some substance when it was made, but that the question had been overtaken by the disposal of the civil revision. The leave sought was therefore declined, and the trial court was told to decide the suit quickly.

The trial court restrained the defendant from entering the land or changing its character, and the appellate court affirmed that order. RESPONDENTs are the plaintiffs. explanation: The court found that both sides had been litigating over an interim order for years while the suit itself had made no progress, and that the injunction as framed would have restrained the defendant over land whose title was yet to be decided. It therefore effaced the injunction, but held that leaving the parties free to alter the position would prejudice the very subject matter of the suit. Instead it directed both sides to hold the existing position over possession of the land, and directed the trial court to decide the suit within one year.

During the hearing of his appeal the parties reported an amicable settlement, the amount having been paid, and jointly asked that the conviction be effaced.
explanation: The court read the revisional application along with the compromise petition, the judgment under appeal and the submissions of both sides, and found it established that the amount claimed had been paid and that neither party had any claim left against the other. It observed that the object of a proceeding of this kind is recovery of the amount, which had been settled between the parties, so that the conviction could not be maintained. The appeal was acceded to on the basis of the compromise, the conviction and sentence were effaced, and the appellant was acquitted.

input_summary: PETITIONER is a pre-emptor who sought pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act over land in Satkhira, saying that he is a co-sharer by inheritance in the holding and that the vendee is a stranger who bought it without his knowledge. The trial court acceded to the pre-emption case and the appellate court reversed it, holding that the land is homestead and so outside the section. RESPONDENT is the vendee. The pre-emptor seeks restoration of the order in his favour, contending that the land was never shown to be homestead.
act: Other: State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950
explanation: The court examined the settlement and survey records and the definition of homestead in the statute, which includes a dwelling house with the land under it and the adjoining courtyard, garden, tank and outbuildings, and found the land to be homestead on the documentary material. It held that the statutory provision expressly excludes homestead land from its operation, so that a pre-emption case over such land is not maintainable at all, whatever the pre-emptor's status as a co-sharer may be. The appellate order was accordingly affirmed and the rule failed.

This Rule was issued calling upon opposite party No. 1 to show 
cause as to why judgment and order dated 08.06.2017 passed by Orpito 
Sompotti Prottarpon Additional Appellate Tribunal and learned 
Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Chattogram in Orpito Appeal No. 24 
of 2016 disallowing the appeal and affirming an order dated 12.06.2016 
passed by Orpito Sompotti Prottarpon Additional Tribunal, Patiya, 
Chattogram in Orpito Sompotti Tribunal Case No. 11110 of 2012 
rejecting an application for addition of party should not be set aside.   
 
At the time of issuance of Rule this Court vide order dated 
26.10.2017 stayed further proceedings of the Tribunal case for a period 
of 03 (three) months which, was, subsequently extended till disposal of 
the Rule. 
Facts relevant, for the purpose of disposal of this Rule, are that 
opposite party No. 1 filed the aforesaid Orpito Sompotti Prottarpon 

<<PAGE 2>>
 
 
 
 
 
2 
 
Case No. 11110 of 2012 for releasing the suit property from the ‘Ka’ list 
of vested properties published in Bangladesh Gazette. 
During pendency of the case, the petitioner filed an application 
under section 25 of Orpito Sompotti Prottarpon Ain, 2001 for adding 
her as a party to the case claiming to be owner of the suit property. 
Opposite party No. 1 filed written objection to contest the application 
and the Tribunal, after herring the parties, vide order dated 12.06.2016 
rejected the application against which the petitioner preferred Orpito 
Sompotti Prottarpon Appeal Tribunal Case No. 24 of 2016 before the 
Orpito Sompotti Prottarpon Appellate Tribunal, Chattogram which was 
then transferred to Orpito Sompotti Prottarpon Additional Appellate 
Tribunal and 6th Court of Additional District Judge, Chattogram for 
disposal who, after hearing the parties,  by impugned judgment dated 
08.06.2017 disallowed the appeal against which the petitioner has 
come up with this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil 
Procedure and obtained the instant Rule and order of stay, as stated 
above. 
This matter was fixed for hearing at the instance the opposite 
party on 19.05.2024 and thereafter, the matter has appeared in the 
daily cause list for hearing for a number of days and today the matter is 
taken up for hearing but the learned Advocate for the petitioner is 
found absent.   
Since the matter involves only question of law we are inclined to 
dispose of this matter in the absence of the learned Advocate for the 
petitioner. 
Mr. Ajoy Shankar Bhowmik, learned Advocate appearing for 
opposite party No. 1 submits that there is no scope under Orpito 
Sompotti Prottarpon Ain, 2001 to add any party to the proceeding 

<<PAGE 3>>
 
 
 
 
 
3 
 
initiated by an aggrieved party for release of the Orpito Sompotti and if 
any party is aggrieved by the publication of the Gazette Notification he 
has to file independent application/case for releasing the said property 
from the Gazette. The petitioner by claiming title to the suit property 
filed application for addition of party to the proceeding initiated by 
opposite party No. 1 and as such, the application is not tenable under 
law. Learned Advocate further submits that as per provision of section 
22(3) of the Orpito Sompotti Prottarpon Tribunal Ain, 2001 the decision 
of the Appellate Tribunal is final and accordingly, this revision is not 
maintainable, also. 
We have heard the learned Advocate, perused the revisional 
application along with the orders passed by the Courts below and the 
grounds taken in the revisional application. In the grounds it have been 
stated that the Appellate Tribunal illegally disallowed the appeal 
without considering the case of the petitioner and as such, interference 
is called for by this Court.  
It appears that as per section 10 of Orpito Sompotti Prottarpon 
Ain, 2001 the claimant of the property published in the schedule ‘Ka’ of 
the Gazette published under section 9 of the Ain, may file application 
within 300 days before the Tribunal by enclosing relevant supporting 
documents for releasing the property. By amendment, said period of 
300 days for filing application has been extended till 31.12.2013. In the 
instant case, opposite party No. 1 by claiming the suit property, filed 
the application for releasing it from the ‘Ka’ list of the Gazette 
Notification. On the other hand, by claiming the same property the 
present petitioner has filed the application for addition of party in the 
proceeding initiated by opposite party No. 1. It appears that conflicting 

<<PAGE 4>>
 
 
 
 
 
4 
 
question of title would arise if the petitioner is added as party to the 
proceeding.  
The Orpito Sompotti Prottarpon Tribunal has vested with the 
power to decide whether any property has been legally enlisted as 
vested property or not and it has got no jurisdiction to decide any 
conflicting title between rival parties. As such, there is no scope under 
the law to add any party to a proceeding initiated by any other party 
under Orpito Sompotti Prottarpon Ain, 2001. So the petitioner has no 
locus standi to file application for adding her as party to the proceeding 
initiated by opposite party No. 1.  
Moreover, as per section 22 (3) of the Orpito Sompotti 
Prottarpon Ain, 2001 the decision of the Appellate Tribunal is final 
which cannot be challenged under revisional jurisdiction. In that score 
also, this revisional application is not maintainable.  
Considering the facts and circumstance of the case and relevant 
provision of law, we find no merit in this Rule. 
In the result, the Rule is discharged however, without any order 
as to costs. 
The order of stay granted earlier is hereby recalled and vacated. 
The concerned Tribunal is directed to proceed with the case in 
accordance with law.  
 
Communicate a copy of this judgment to the Court below at 
once.  
  
 
 
 
   
 
(Justice Md. Badruzzaman)  
 
 
 
I agree. 
  
         
 
 
        (Mr. Justice Sashanka Shekhar Sarkar)
input_summary: PETITIONER is a claimant who applied to be added as a party in a proceeding before the tribunal on transfer of vested property, in which another person sought to have the land released from the list of vested property published in the gazette. The tribunal and the appellate tribunal both turned her application down. RESPONDENT is the applicant in the main proceeding. The petitioner seeks reversal of those orders, contending that as a rival claimant of the same land she should have been heard before any order releasing the property was made.
explanation: The court examined the scheme of the statute and found that the tribunal is vested only with the power to decide whether a property has been lawfully listed as vested property, and that it has no jurisdiction to decide a question of conflicting title between rival claimants. It held that where the petitioner's claim would raise precisely such a conflict, there was no scope under the law for adding her as a party to a proceeding begun by another, and that she lacked the standing to apply. It also noted that the decision of the appellate tribunal is final under the statute and cannot be challenged in revision.

The provisions under sections 13 and 14 of the Arbitration Act,

stated about the disqualifications of an arbitrator for which a party to

According to sub-section (1) read with sub-section (2) of section 
15 of the Arbitration Act, 2001, the mandate of an arbitrator shall 
terminate, if  
(a)  he withdraws himself from his office;  
(b)  he dies;  
(c)  all the parties agree on the termination of his mandate; 
or  
(d) he is unable to perform his functions of his office or for 
other reasons fails to act without undue delay and 
withdraws from his office or the parties agree on the 
termination of his mandate.  
If any arbitrator has incurred disqualifications referred to in 
clause- (d) of sub-section (1) of section 15 of the Act, the District Judge, 
in case of other arbitrations excepting international commercial 
arbitration, and the Chief Justice or a Judge of the Supreme Court 
designated by the Chief Justice in case of international commercial 
arbitration, on the application by any party may terminate the said 
arbitrator.  
The disqualifications as stated in Clause – ‘d’ of sub-section (1) of 
section 15 of the Act of 2001 has not been defined in the Arbitration 
Act. As per said Clause disqualification means ‘if the arbitrator is unable 
to perform his functions of his office or for other reasons fails to act 
without undue delay and withdraws from his office’.  “Unable to 
perform his function is a big term which includes unable to work at all, 
unable to perform any one of the essential functions of his or her 
position i.e the fundamental job duties of the employment position and 
a manifest  lack of qualities. 

<<PAGE 9>>
 
 
 
 
 
9 
 
Rule 14 of the ICSID Convention Arbitration Rules 2022 specifies 
the qualities required of the Arbitrators. They must possess high moral 
Character, recognized competence in the fields of law, commerce, 
industry or finance who may be relied upon to exercise independent 
judgment. The most frequently proposed ground for disqualification of 
a member of a Tribunal is alleged lake of reliability to exercise 
independent or impartial judgment. An Arbitrator may also be removed 
for incapacity or failure to perform the duties required of an arbitrator. 
In the instant case, the land owners and developer entered into 
development agreement and as per terms of that agreement the 
developer started to construct building in the land owned by the 
petitioner and two others but admittedly, could not complete the 
construction work in stipulated time for which the land-owners 
sustained financial loss. The developer alleges that the land owners 
forcibly dispossessed them from a portion of the constructed building 
before completion of the project and accordingly, the developer 
incurred huge financial loss. The land owners also claimed that the land 
in question was under mortgage in financial institution and tri-partied 
agreement was executed among the developer, land owners and the 
bank for repayment outstanding dues of the land owners from the 
proceeds of the constructed flats but since the developer could not 
complete the project within specified time and violated the tri-partied 
agreement and did not pay the installments to the bank as per the 
agreement  the land owners rightly took possession of some portion of 
the under constructed and unfinished building. To resolve the dispute,   
arbitrators were appointed by the learned District Judge. Accordingly, it 
was the duty of the arbitrators to assess the cost incurred by the 
developer and the loss of the land-owners for non-completion of the 

<<PAGE 10>>
 
 
 
 
 
10 
 
project in stipulated time. How the cost of the unfinished constructed 
building would be determined ? Is it possible by local inspection? 
Answer is obviously no. But the arbitrators instead of allowing the 
application for local investigation for ascertaining the actual cost, loss 
and damage appointed themselves as local inspectors to see the 
building only and not to determine the actual loss or profit or expense 
or expenditure of the building or the measurement of the unfinished 
constructed building. A local inspection cannot determine the actual 
loss or expense or cost of the building and accordingly, the arbitrators 
should have allowed the application for local investigation. It is also 
against the norms of judicial practices that the arbitrators themselves 
would collect the evidence by way of local inspection. It is one kind of 
misconduct on the part of the arbitrators. Moreover, the Arbitrators did 
not frame any issue to resolve the dispute and after inspection they did 
not supply any inspection report to either of the parties but directed to 
pay cost for preparing arbitral award. Accordingly, we are of the view 
that the members of the arbitral tribunal were unable to perform their 
functions of their office as per law and also failed to act without undue 
delay because of the fact that the tribunal was constituted in 2019  and 
it  could not give any award till 15.10.2023, the date of passing the 
impugned order and they did not withdrawn from their office and 
accordingly, such disqualifications, as stated above, fell within the 
preview of “he is unable to perform his functions of his office or for the 
reasons fails to act without undue delay” as stated in clause ‘(d)’ of sub-
section (1) of section 15 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 and as such, the 
application filed by the land-owners before the learned District Judge 
was maintainable.  

<<PAGE 11>>
 
 
 
 
 
11 
 
It appears that the learned District Judge without considering 
above aspect of the matter illegally rejected the application filed by the 
land owners. We are of the view that the dispute between the parties 
should be resolved by appointing fresh arbitrators who are competent 
to resolve the dispute in the prevailing facts and circumstances of the 
case.  
In that view of the matter we find merit in this Rule. 
In the result, the Rule is made Absolute. The impugned order 
dated 15.10.2023 is hereby set aside. The mandate of the arbitrators is 
terminated. 
The learned District Judge is directed to appoint another arbitral 
tribunal consisting of three members to resolve the dispute between 
the parties afresh. The Chairman of the tribunal will be selected by the 
learned District Judge from the retired District Judges. Out of other two 
members, one will be appointed by the choice of the land owners and 
another by the choice of the developer company.      
The order of stay and status-quo granted earlier is hereby 
vacated.  
 
Communicate a copy of this judgment to the Court below at 
once.  
 
  
 
 
 
   
 
(Justice Md. Badruzzaman)  
 
 
 
I agree. 
 
  
         
 
 
        (Mr. Justice Sashanka Shekhar Sarkar)
input_summary: PETITIONER is one of several owners of about 0.4 acre of land in Chattogram who entered into a development agreement with a real estate company in 2010, followed by a fresh agreement in 2019, for a multi-storied building which the developer failed to complete in time. The owners applied to the District Judge for the mandate of the arbitral tribunal to be terminated, the tribunal having been constituted in 2019 without giving any award by 2023, and the application was turned down. RESPONDENT is the developer. The owners seek reversal of that order.
explanation: The court found that the tribunal had been constituted in 2019 and had not produced an award by October 2023, when the order under challenge was passed, and that its members had not withdrawn from office. It held that such a failure fell squarely within the statutory ground that an arbitrator is unable to perform his functions or fails to act without undue delay, so that the application to the District Judge was maintainable and the refusal to entertain it was wrong. The rule succeeded, the mandate was terminated, and a fresh three-member tribunal was directed to be constituted.
